## Proof

Let $K \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$ for some $\lambda > 0$, let $r_1, r_2, \dots$ be i.i.d. with $r_i \sim N(0,1)$, independent of $K$, and let
$$Z = \sum_{i=1}^{K} r_i.$$

**Cumulant generating function of a compound Poisson sum.**

By conditioning on $K$ and using the independence of $K$ and the $r_i$,
$$M_Z(t) = \mathbb{E}[e^{tZ}] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{t\sum_{i=1}^{K} r_i} \,\middle|\, K\right]\right] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[(M_r(t))^{K}\right] = \exp\!\big(\lambda(M_r(t)-1)\big).$$

Hence the cumulant generating function (cgf) of $Z$ is
$$K_Z(t) = \log M_Z(t) = \lambda\big(M_r(t) - 1\big).$$

**Moment generating function of the jump distribution.**

Since $r \sim N(0,1)$,
$$M_r(t) = \mathbb{E}[e^{tr}] = \exp\!\left(\tfrac{t^{2}}{2}\right).$$

**Substitution.**

Therefore
$$K_Z(t) = \lambda\!\left(\exp\!\left(\tfrac{t^{2}}{2}\right) - 1\right).$$

Expanding the exponential,
$$\exp\!\left(\tfrac{t^{2}}{2}\right) - 1 = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k!}\left(\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right)^{k} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{t^{2k}}{2^{k}\, k!}.$$

Thus
$$K_Z(t) = \lambda \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{t^{2k}}{2^{k}\, k!} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{\lambda}{2^{k}\, k!}\, t^{2k}.$$

**Reading off the cumulants.**

By definition the $n$-th cumulant $\kappa_n$ is the coefficient of $\frac{t^{n}}{n!}$ in $K_Z(t)$:
$$K_Z(t) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \kappa_n \frac{t^{n}}{n!}.$$

The series we obtained contains **only even powers** $t^{2k}$; every odd power $t^{2k+1}$ has coefficient $0$. Equivalently, for odd $n = 2k+1$,
$$\kappa_{2k+1} = (2k+1)!\cdot [t^{2k+1}]\, K_Z(t) = (2k+1)!\cdot 0 = 0.$$

For completeness, the even-order cumulants are
$$\kappa_{2k} = (2k)!\cdot \frac{\lambda}{2^{k}\, k!}, \qquad k = 1, 2, \dots$$

**Conclusion.**

The cumulant generating function $K_Z(t) = \lambda\big(e^{t^{2}/2} - 1\big)$ is an even function of $t$ (it depends on $t$ only through $t^{2}$). The cumulants are the Taylor coefficients of $K_Z$ (up to the factorial normalization), and an even function has vanishing Taylor coefficients at all odd orders. Therefore

$$\boxed{\kappa_{n} = 0 \quad \text{for every odd } n = 1, 3, 5, \dots}$$

i.e., **all cumulants of odd order of the compound Poisson distribution with $N(0,1)$ jumps are zero.**
